==Problem==

A rectangular garden 60 feet long and 20 feet wide is enclosed by a fence. To make the garden larger, while using the same fence, its shape is changed to a square. By how many square feet does this enlarge the garden?

<imath>\text{(A)}\ 100 \qquad \text{(B)}\ 200 \qquad \text{(C)}\ 300 \qquad \text{(D)}\ 400 \qquad \text{(E)}\ 500</imath>

==Solution 1==

We need the same perimeter as a <imath>60</imath> by <imath>20</imath> rectangle, but the greatest area we can get. right now the perimeter is <imath>160</imath>. To get the greatest area while keeping a perimeter of <imath>160</imath>, the sides should all be <imath>40</imath>. that means an area of <imath>1600</imath>. Right now, the area is <imath>20 \times 60</imath> which is <imath>1200</imath>. <imath>1600-1200=400</imath> which is <imath>\boxed{D}</imath>.
==Solution 2==
We need the same perimeter as a <imath>60</imath> by <imath>20</imath> rectangle, but in a square. Right now the perimeter is <imath>160</imath>, since a square has equal sides and <imath>160</imath> divided by 4 is <imath>40</imath>,  the sides should all be <imath>40</imath>, that means an area of <imath>1600</imath>. Before, the area is <imath>20 \times 60</imath> which is <imath>1200</imath>. <imath>1600-1200=400</imath> which is <imath>\boxed{D}</imath>.
